land.text: the Ertebølle country, where the Funnelbeaker 'replaced the Ertebølle culture' in southern Scandinavia and whose northern group is 'roughly the area that previously belonged to the Ertebølle-Ellerbek complex'

successors.note: The funnelbeaker-culture dossier starts at -4100 and already holds this land (Denmark, Schleswig-Holstein, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Skane and more) with counterpart 'nobody'; the Ertebølle's infobox end is -3950, so the two overlap -4100..-3950 and a ruling or the size rule must settle it. The funnelbeaker dossier records no loss from the Ertebølle.

correction.text: southern Scandinavia, where the culture 'was concentrated': Denmark (the type site is in Jutland) and Schleswig-Holstein ('the Ellerbek culture of Schleswig-Holstein', 'approximately identical') with southern Sweden (drawn: Skane, Halland and Blekinge; the page names only the population of Scania)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Ertebølle row. Infobox 'c. 5,400 BCE - c. 3,950 BCE'; 'The culture was concentrated in Southern Scandinavia'; the page gives no area and no site count. Shape: Denmark, Schleswig-Holstein, Skane, Halland and Blekinge, 368 cells, about 93,100 km2 by the gazetteer. The page names Scania only in a hypothesis about origins and gives the northern limit only as 'the Scandinavian Nøstvet and Lihult cultures', so southern Sweden is the researcher's reading. The Funnelbeaker page says the northern TRB group is 'roughly the area that previously belonged to the Ertebølle-Ellerbek complex', which is much wider (Lower Saxony to Uppland); not adopted because it describes the TRB and not the Ertebølle. One shape for 1,300 years: the page's early phase 'c. 5,400 BCE - c. 4,500 BCE' and later phase 'c. 4,500 BCE - 3,950 BCE' have no stated change of extent.

correction.text: southern Scandinavia, where the culture 'was concentrated': Denmark (the type site is in Jutland) and Schleswig-Holstein ('the Ellerbek culture of Schleswig-Holstein', 'approximately identical') with southern Sweden (drawn: Skane, Halland and Blekinge; the page names only the population of Scania); plus the German Baltic coast: 'Shortly after 4,100 BCE the Ertebølle began to expand along the Baltic coast at least as far as Rügen' (drawn as discs at Wismar, Rostock and Stralsund)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Shortly after 4,100 BCE the Ertebølle began to expand along the Baltic coast at least as far as Rügen'; 57 more cells (about 14,400 km2) for the coast, 425 cells and about 107,500 km2 in all by the gazetteer. The Funnelbeaker dossier draws all of this land from -4100; the page says only 'Shortly thereafter it was replaced by the Funnelbeaker culture' (no year; infobox end -3950).

ledger.note: 5400 BCE: the Ertebølle culture appears in southern Scandinavia. Infobox 'c. 5,400 BCE - c. 3,950 BCE', 'Preceded by: Kongemose culture'; it 'replaced the earlier Kongemose culture of Denmark' and 'was concentrated in Southern Scandinavia'; 'the Ellerbek culture of Schleswig-Holstein' is 'approximately identical'. The page gives the countries, not a boundary, so the whole range is drawn from the start and the extent is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the German Baltic coast: 'Shortly after 4,100 BCE the Ertebølle began to expand along the Baltic coast at least as far as Rügen' (drawn as discs at Wismar, Rostock and Stralsund)

ledger.note: 4100 BCE: the Ertebølle spreads along the Baltic coast to Rügen. 'Shortly after 4,100 BCE the Ertebølle began to expand along the Baltic coast at least as far as Rügen'. The page gives the year only as 'shortly after' and no boundary; it is silent on who held the coast, so the land is recorded as nobody's.

Ertebølle infobox end 'c. 3,950 BCE', 'Followed by: Funnelbeaker culture', 'Shortly thereafter it was replaced by the Funnelbeaker culture'; Funnelbeaker page: 'In southern Scandinavia it replaced the Ertebølle culture, which had maintained a Mesolithic lifestyle for about 1500 years after farming arrived in Central Europe'; the Funnelbeaker begins 'c. 4100 BCE' (its infobox), so the funnelbeaker-culture dossier already holds the land 150 years earlier.

notes:
Ertebølle culture (c. 5,400-3,950 BCE, southern Scandinavia), typed culture like the funnelbeaker-culture dossier; Cliopatria has no row. Three pages opened.

To settle: (1) Overlap with the funnelbeaker-culture dossier, which starts -4100 on this land (counterpart nobody) while the Ertebølle's infobox ends -3950: 150 years in which both are drawn; the size rule or a ruling must settle which is drawn (the Ertebølle shape here is about 107,500 km2 at most). The Ertebølle page itself says the culture expanded along the coast after 4100 and was replaced 'shortly thereafter' with no year, which fits neither 4100 nor 3950 exactly. (2) Kongemose culture (circa 6,000-5,200 BCE, Denmark and Skåne) has no dossier and overlaps the Ertebølle's first 200 years in the pages' dates. The Swifterbant culture (5,300-3,400 BCE, Noordoostpolder, 'related') has no dossier and is not drawn. (3) The page gives no extent for Sweden or Norway beyond 'Southern Scandinavia' and the 'Scandinavian Nøstvet and Lihult cultures' to the north; southern Sweden is drawn as Skåne, Halland and Blekinge. Mecklenburg-Vorpommern is not named (only the Baltic coast to Rügen). Poland/Pomerania and southern Norway are not on the page. (4) The Funnelbeaker page describes the northern TRB group as 'roughly the area that previously belonged to the Ertebølle-Ellerbek complex'; if a reviewer prefers that wider shape for the Ertebølle, it is the northern part of the funnelbeaker-culture -4100 shape. (5) Native name Ertebøllekulturen is the standard Danish name, not read from the page text returned. (6) Slug: tools/slug.py slugify('Ertebølle culture') gives 'erteb-lle-culture' (the validator warns); the brief's slug 'ertebolle-culture' is kept as instructed and the orchestrator may rename. (7) Gazetteer names used (Wismar, Rostock, Stralsund and the admin1 units) all resolve.
